meta.title: Telugu A1 Beginner
meta.subtitle: 500 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Telugu → English (see the Telugu, recall the meaning) and English → Telugu (see an English meaning, recall the Telugu). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 500 words for a beginner, aligned to A1 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand and use familiar everyday expressions and very basic phrases aimed at the satisfaction of needs of a concrete type' — a learner here is able to introduce themselves and others, to ask and answer questions about personal details such as where they live, people they know and things they have, and to interact in a simple way provided the other person talks slowly and clearly and is prepared to help. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: no exam board publishes a graded word list for Telugu, so this deck is not any examination's vocabulary and does not claim to be. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 276 of the 500 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — greetings and politeness, introducing yourself, family, numbers, telling the time, the days of the week, food and drink, shopping and money, the home, the town and getting about, the body and feeling ill, the weather, colours, and the pronouns, question words, place words and conjunctions every sentence is built out of — and the other 224 are the commonest remaining words in a frequency list built from film and television subtitles, with the words the subtitles' machine translation had garbled taken out by hand. The cards are dealt by that frequency, so the words you meet most often come first. Every word is a dictionary word: one that English Wiktionary does not have was left out rather than given a meaning, which is why a few everyday loanwords are missing. Verbs are given in their dictionary form, the one ending in -u (తిను tinu, 'to eat'). Every headword is printed in Telugu script with a romanisation beneath it, Wiktionary's own (ā ē ō for the long vowels, ṭ ḍ ṇ ḷ for the retroflex letters), so the deck can be studied before the script is fluent; the Telugu Alphabet deck, the first in this collection, teaches the script itself. The 304 nouns show their gender where Wiktionary records it, and their plural; where Wiktionary has their tables, verbs show their past and future and behind the All forms fold their present continuous, past and future by person, and nouns their six cases. Real example sentences come with 96 of the 500 words — Tatoeba holds only a few hundred Telugu sentences with an English translation — with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings, gender, forms and romanisation: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
